daily.summary: The past day's reporting is led by two FBI alerts: one on ARTEX, an AI framework used to automate intrusions against several critical sectors, and one attributing a $400 million crypto-theft scheme to North Korean state hackers. CISA urged immediate patching of a critical Java flaw dubbed Java4Shell, for which no exploitation has been reported so far, and listed a Cisco BroadWorks bug that researchers say was used against a European telecom provider. Romania confirmed it contained a Russian Turla intrusion into government email, and newly disclosed flaws in Copeland refrigeration controllers are already being probed.

weekly.summary: The week's reporting centres on attackers using AI to speed up intrusions: the FBI, Google and Unit 42 all describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations, and Google says Chinese state groups are building their own. State-linked activity this week includes North Korean financial theft, Russian espionage against Romanian government email, and a reported China-linked intrusion at a European telecom provider through a Cisco BroadWorks flaw. Patching pressure is high, with a critical Java flaw and newly disclosed refrigeration controller bugs both drawing official or researcher warnings. No confirmed disruption of US or allied critical infrastructure was reported in this window.
